messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: New features for Shiny 0.8.0
parts:
Hi all,

We're hoping to submit Shiny 0.8.0 to CRAN very shortly, and would love your feedback on some of the new features that we've added since 0.7.0. Please help us by installing and testing the latest version from GitHub:

    if (!require(devtools))
      install.packages('devtools')
    install.packages('httpuv')
    devtools::install_github('shiny', 'rstudio')

RStudio users should also install the latest v0.98.443 Preview Release, which is available here: http://www.rstudio.com/ide/download/preview

New debugging features

In this release of Shiny we've greatly improved the set of debugging tools you can use with your Shiny apps. It's now much easier to figure out what's happening when things go wrong, thanks to two new features:
  • Integration with the new visual debugger that's available with RStudio v0.98. You can set breakpoints and step through your code much more easily than before.
  • A new option 'shiny.error' which can take a function as an error handler. It is called when an error occurs in a reactive observer (e.g. when running an output rendering function). You can use options(shiny.error=traceback) to simply print a traceback, options(shiny.error=recover) for debugging from a regular R console, or options(shiny.error=browser) to jump into the RStudio visual debugger.
We're especially interested in feedback for these debugging features -- please do try them and let us know whether you find them useful!

DataTables integration

Shiny 0.8.0 will support much more attractive and powerful displays of tabular data using the popular DataTables library. Our DataTables integration features pagination, searching/filtering, sorting, and more. Check out this demo to see it in action, and learn more about how to use it in your own apps by visiting the tutorial's chapter on DataTables (you may need to refresh your web browser if you cannot see this chapter).

There have also been a few smaller tweaks and bug fixes. For the full list, you can take a look at our NEWS file (you see v0.7.0.99 there but it will turn to v0.8.0 on CRAN).

Thanks for your support -- we look forward to hearing from you!

-- The Shiny team

messages.author: 5893d17d64b5b0c2
messages.subject: Re: New features for Shiny 0.8.0
parts:
Hi Stephane,

Thanks for the feedback, these are great finds! 

Some workarounds for now, if these are hampering your productivity:

1) If your breakpoints seem out of sync with the document, restarting the R session should fix the problem (use Session -> Restart R) 

2) If there are so many environments in the drop list that you can't pick the one you want, you can remove items you don't need from the list. What's displayed there is effectively the output of search() plus debug context environments, so you can trim it down by using detach() to remove package environments. 

I've filed a couple of internal bugs based on the problems you've found, and we hope to have them fixed soon.

Thanks,
Jonathan.

On Tuesday, October 22, 2013 12:05:23 PM UTC-7, Yihui Xie wrote:
Hi all,

We're hoping to submit Shiny 0.8.0 to CRAN very shortly, and would love your feedback on some of the new features that we've added since 0.7.0. Please help us by installing and testing the latest version from GitHub:

    if (!require(devtools))
      install.packages('devtools')
    install.packages('httpuv')
    devtools::install_github('shiny', 'rstudio')

RStudio users should also install the latest v0.98.443 Preview Release, which is available here: http://www.rstudio.com/ide/download/preview

New debugging features

In this release of Shiny we've greatly improved the set of debugging tools you can use with your Shiny apps. It's now much easier to figure out what's happening when things go wrong, thanks to two new features:
  • Integration with the new visual debugger that's available with RStudio v0.98. You can set breakpoints and step through your code much more easily than before.
  • A new option 'shiny.error' which can take a function as an error handler. It is called when an error occurs in a reactive observer (e.g. when running an output rendering function). You can use options(shiny.error=traceback) to simply print a traceback, options(shiny.error=recover) for debugging from a regular R console, or options(shiny.error=browser) to jump into the RStudio visual debugger.
We're especially interested in feedback for these debugging features -- please do try them and let us know whether you find them useful!

DataTables integration

Shiny 0.8.0 will support much more attractive and powerful displays of tabular data using the popular DataTables library. Our DataTables integration features pagination, searching/filtering, sorting, and more. Check out this demo to see it in action, and learn more about how to use it in your own apps by visiting the tutorial's chapter on DataTables (you may need to refresh your web browser if you cannot see this chapter).

There have also been a few smaller tweaks and bug fixes. For the full list, you can take a look at our NEWS file (you see v0.7.0.99 there but it will turn to v0.8.0 on CRAN).

Thanks for your support -- we look forward to hearing from you!

-- The Shiny team
